representation_assessment.B_continuous_unwrapped: Satisfies the invariant if every geographic constructor re-anchors its result to the current state before interpolation.
representation_assessment.C_explicit_shortest_arc: Satisfies a single interval, but continuation and multi-key orbit rings still require a coherent accumulated frame.
representation_assessment.D_behavioral_authority: Continuous longitude modulo 360° is authoritative for motion; wrapped longitude is an external serialization representation only.

B_orbit_altitude_owns_boundary.staging: The complete boundary pose equals the successor orbit pose.

C_arrival_transition_interpolates_to_orb.staging: The moving segment absorbs the pose change and lands at the orbit pose.

D_joint_pose_solved_from_target.staging: There is no unique joint solution until the preserved variables (altitude, ring footprint, tilt, or screen framing) are named.

partially_spherical.finding: The single-axis shortcut makes every equal-latitude leg linear in longitude regardless of length. Those paths follow a parallel, not the great-circle geodesic (except at the equator). Arrival endpoints remain correct.

approach_point.consequence: Production adds a position key at 80% of the staged move, approaching from behind the orbit tangent. Dirty/Codex compute the candidate point but deliberately do not emit it, so the whole movement is controlled by their replacement path/final endpoint. It affects staging direction and incoming velocity; it is not a seam guard. Across the antimeridian, production re-anchors this approach longitude and therefore confines the wrapped-endpoint lap to the final span, while the variants can expose the whole leg to the wrapped endpoint.
